Messages.Author: REED J G
Messages.Body:
When a vampire enters torpor untapped, does it untap with all other
cards in the untap phase?

And....

When the trap card is played, it is played that three rounds of combat
then take place, and no Methuselah is allowed to play cards on their
vampires, or are you allowed to play cards, with three rounds at the end
with no cards to be played. I believe that it should be three rounds of
combat with no cards allowed whatsoever.

Thanks for any replies.

Jason G. Reed

>When a vampire enters torpor untapped, does it untap with all other

>And....

>When the trap card is played, it is played that three rounds of combat

>vampires, or are you allowed to play cards, with three rounds at the end

Sorry, but the latter is correct.

Messages.Author: James Puzzo
Messages.Body:
REED J G (c922...@alinga.newcastle.edu.au) wrote:

: When the trap card is played, it is played that three rounds of combat

: then take place, and no Methuselah is allowed to play cards on their
: vampires, or are you allowed to play cards, with three rounds at the end
: with no cards to be played. I believe that it should be three rounds of
: combat with no cards allowed whatsoever.

Pretty much the second interpretation. In other words, the minion that
plays the trap has a press to continue every round until three rounds
have passed in which NO ONE has played any cards. One may, of course,
still press to end during the press phase of any of these trapped rounds.

-James

Messages.Author: Super Ted
Messages.Body:
>When a vampire enters torpor untapped, does it untap with
all other
>cards in the untap phase?

Vampires may untap in torpor as normal.

>When the trap card is played, it is played that three rounds
of combat
>then take place, and no Methuselah is allowed to play cards
on their
>vampires, or are you allowed to play cards, with three
rounds at the end
>with no cards to be played. I believe that it should be
three rounds of
>combat with no cards allowed whatsoever.

When a trap is played, combat automatically has a press to
continue for three rounds. However, if any card should be
played in the combat then the terms of the trap start again,
i.e. Combat automatically has a press to continue for three
rounds. In effect this means that with a trap, combat tends
to last for a LONG time - usually resulting with one of the
minions in torpor.

Peter
